title: South Korea expands crypto market probes after $44B Bithumb Bitcoin blunder
summary: South Korea’s financial watchdog detailed planned investigations into high-risk trading tactics as it prepares the next phase of crypto regulation, Yonhap News Agency reported.

title: BTC traders wait for $50K bottom: Five things to know in Bitcoin this week
summary: Bitcoin price forecasts retained odds of new macro lows next as risk asset traders remained nervous about US and Japan macroeconomic tailwinds.

title: Coinbase bets on Backstreet Boys nostalgia in return to Super Bowl
summary: Coinbase’s TV spot at the Super Bowl divided opinion online, but the crypto exchange says conversations about it were the point.

title: ENS abandons plans for Namechain L2, citing Ethereum scaling
summary: Citing a 99% drop in gas fees and upcoming Ethereum scaling, the project will now deploy its ENSv2 upgrade directly on Ethereum.

title: Bitcoin Sharpe ratio slides to levels seen in previous market bottoms
summary: Bitcoin’s Sharpe ratio has fallen to -10, nearing bear market lows seen in 2018 and 2022, suggesting the risk/reward profile is approaching extreme levels.

title: Crypto.com CEO unveils new AI agents to millions during Super Bowl
summary: Crypto.com CEO Kris Marszalek’s goal with ai.com is to build “a decentralized network of autonomous, self-improving AI agents that perform real-world tasks for the good of humanity.”

title: Bessent suggests Warsh nomination hearings alongside Powell probe
summary: The Fed chair confirmation faces a key hurdle as a senator vows to block the process until a DOJ investigation into Jerome Powell is resolved.

title: Crypto and banks spar in comments on Fed’s ‘skinny master account’ idea
summary: Crypto companies have backed a Federal Reserve proposal to give them limited access to the central bank, while banking associations have urged caution.

title: Address poisoning recently cost 2 victims over $62M alone: Scam Sniffer
summary: Analysts have warned that Ethereum’s Fusaka upgrade has made address poisoning cheaper, as malicious actors can carry out dust attacks for very little cost.

title: Only 10K Bitcoin at quantum risk and worth attacking, CoinShares claims
summary: Most quantum-vulnerable Bitcoin sits in wallets holding under 100 Bitcoin, with CoinShares claiming it could take a millennium to compromise each one.
